last_3_hypotheses: BGE-M3 underperforms on game-theory abstracts because the field's terminology is highly domain-specific and the M3 training distribution under-represents game-theory papers.
ChromaDB k-NN queries on collections smaller than ~500 documents are slower than a brute-force cosine over the same set because the HNSW index overhead dominates.
Run-log entries with status='partial' are not currently scored against any of the Day-7 publication review gate's pass-signals.
proposed_hypothesis_text: BGE-M3 embedding latency in single-document batches is dominated by tokenizer overhead, not by transformer forward time — the per-token cost amortizes correctly only once batch size exceeds about 8 documents.
rationale: Same artifact (BGE-M3) but the prior hypothesis is about quality (retrieval correctness on game-theory abstracts) and the proposed is about latency (tokenizer-overhead dominance at small batch size). These are orthogonal properties of the same model. A meta-reviewer that flags anything-named-BGE-M3 as a duplicate would be over-aggressive.
